chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:
I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) combing with an ivory comb, and I had bought it for him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title for Imam al-Hassan (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam do with an ivory comb?
ai.summary: This brief narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s adherence to the Sunnah of grooming, emphasizing that spiritual leadership does not preclude engagement with worldly comforts and practicalities. The specific mention of the ivory comb (*mushat al-ij*) purchased by the narrator highlights the Imam’s appreciation for quality and the permissibility of using fine materials, reinforcing the Shia view that the Imams exemplify the ideal balance between asceticism and dignified living.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Musa Bin Bakr who said,
‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> combing with an ivory comb, and I had bought it for him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindiy from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “
I saw abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, using ivory comb and I bought it for him.’”
